note: Every name carries a signed edge_score on -100..+100. There is no call and no threshold: rank on edge_score and cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what makes the ranking question answerable at every k.

findings.finding: US energy storage installed a record 20.2 GWh in calendar Q2 2026 (17.9-18.0 GWh utility-scale, 1.8 GWh commercial/industrial), 30.8 GWh in H1, and SEIA/Benchmark RAISED the full-year 2026 forecast to 71 GWh versus 59 GWh installed in 2025 - published 2026-09-01, twelve weeks after ABM last spoke, and covering the two months (May, June) that sit inside ABM's fiscal Q3.
findings.adversary_note: The numbers are correct — I verified 20.2 GWh, 18 GWh utility-scale, 1.8 GWh C&I, and the raise to 71 GWh vs 59 GWh in 2025 in the cited ess-news piece, sourced to the SEIA/Benchmark Q3 2026 Energy Storage Market Outlook. But the claim's headline overstates the ABM-relevant portion by roughly an order of magnitude. ~89% of the record is utility-scale, where ABM/RavenVolt is not a participant; ABM's BESS work is behind-the-meter C&I microgrid, and the same article notes H1 C&I was 'tracking 13% below 2025's total annual deployment' — the segment ABM actually serves is not the record. More decisively, the ABM-specific implication is already management's own published narrative: on 2026-06-05 ABM reported ATS revenue of $267.3m (+27%), said it 'had a really good quarter on the battery energy storage side', announced a major big-box microgrid win, called BESS 'a multiyear growth cycle', and reaffirmed FY26 revenue growth at the top of 4-5% on exactly this driver — and the stock rose 6.67% that day. National install statistics for May-June cannot inform ABM's fiscal Q3 revenue independently of a backlog ABM already described. Finally the sign is ambiguous against consensus: the preview consensus is EPS $1.04 and the whole debate is margin recovery, while management explicitly said these equipment-heavy BESS projects carry compressed margins. A record install quarter is a revenue tailwind and a mix headwind, which is not the trade the claim implies. ATS is 11.5% of revenue.

findings.finding: CBRE's Q2 2026 US office report (2026-07-29) shows national vacancy falling 30bp to 18.3% - 'the largest quarterly decline since 2015' - net absorption of 12.6m sq ft, nearly double the prior quarter and a ninth straight positive quarter, leasing +16% y/y, with CBRE projecting 2026 annual leasing to surpass the 2022 record; San Francisco, the exact market ABM's CEO singled out on 2026-06-05 as having vacancy 'probably 2 or 3x worse than New York City', posted +963,980 sq ft of net absorption in the quarter.
findings.adversary_note: Every figure is right — I confirmed 18.3% vacancy, -30bp, 'the largest quarterly decline since 2015', 12.6m sq ft net absorption and ninth straight positive quarter, leasing +16% y/y to 62.4m sq ft, the projection to surpass 2022, and San Francisco's +963,980 sq ft in CBRE's separate SF Office Figures Q2 2026. Credit for accuracy. Two problems remain. First, publication: CBRE's quarterly US office figures are a staple read for anyone covering facility services, they went out 2026-07-29, and the trade press picked them up — Facilities Dive on 2026-08-04, ULI, and GlobeSt on the San Francisco tech-demand angle on 2026-09-02. Second and larger, the 'gotcha' against the CEO does not land: CBRE's own SF report puts SF vacancy at 29.2%, which still makes the CEO's 2026-06-05 'probably 2 or 3x worse than New York City' true, and he had already told the market on that same call that national net absorption 'turned significantly positive' and was 'the strongest since 2020' with prime vacancy tightening. The direction of travel is in the company's published narrative. Third, transmission barely reaches this print: 12.6m sq ft is ~0.2% of US office stock, and absorption converts to janitorial scope only after build-out and move-in, two to four quarters later — leases signed in calendar Q2 do not touch May-July revenue. Against that, B&I was flat in Q2 and management guided it to 'moderate' on client exits with TfL alone a ~300bp headwind, a company-specific offset that swamps a 30bp national vacancy improvement.

findings.finding: ABM Aviation grew 19.5% in Q2 and its CEO warned on 2026-06-05 that 'rising fuel costs will likely create some near-term challenges for our airline clients'; since then the airline cost shock deepened rather than resolved - American Airlines cut FY26 guidance a second time in July (to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 adjusted EPS range from -$0.40 to +$1.10, with a Q3 loss guide, on ~$3.75/gal fuel), Southwest cut FY26 to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4' after a ~$900m y/y Q2 fuel increase, and Alaska has had guidance suspended since April.
findings.adversary_note: Factually clean — I verified American's 2026-07-23 cut to -$0.65/+$0.65 from -$0.40/+$1.10 on ~$3.75/gal, Southwest's cut to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4' after a ~$900m y/y Q2 fuel increase, and that Alaska suspended full-year guidance in April. But these are not obscure: they are among the most heavily covered corporate events of the summer, and the market's own verdict is on the record — American's stock rose 6.8% the day after it cut, because the fuel shock was already discounted in the airlines themselves. A second-order read-through to a ground-services vendor is strictly less informative than the first-order print that the market shrugged off. On transmission the claim runs the wrong way. Airline pain here is cost, not volume: American's Q2 revenue was +16.3% and Southwest's +20.3%, both records, and ABM's revenue is throughput-driven — management cited TSA throughput near 3m/day and robust leisure demand. ABM Aviation's growth drivers are airport-authority contracts, not airline-funded ones: LaGuardia Terminal B, Heathrow, Orlando International, Miami International. Vendor price pressure from airlines operates on renewal cycles, not inside a single quarter. And the qualitative warning is the company's own, published 2026-06-05 — the day the stock rose 6.67%, so it was not read as a reason to sell. The genuine Aviation risk is margin (6.3% to 5.3% on weather, contract scope changes and TSA-driven disruption), which is company-specific and orthogonal to jet fuel, and which the sell-side preview has already named as the central question for this print.

findings.finding: Note 8 of the Q2 FY26 10-Q states that ABM performed its review of the majority of its casualty insurance programmes during Q2 2026 and 'it was determined that there was no adjustment required for our total reserves related to prior years during the six months ended April 30, 2026' - so the item that produced a $(22.2)m pre-tax hit (~100bp of adjusted EBITDA margin, ~$0.26/sh) in Q4 FY25 is a Q2/Q4 event and is very unlikely to appear in the Q3 print, even though ABM's adjusted EPS definition now includes it while its guidance range is stated 'before any impact from prior-year self-insurance adjustments'.
findings.adversary_note: Every element is factually correct and I want to say that plainly: the $(22.2)m pre-tax Q4 FY25 hit, the ~100bp adjusted EBITDA margin effect and the $(0.26)/sh are in ABM's own Q4 FY25 release; the SEC did force ABM to stop excluding prior-year self-insurance adjustments from adjusted EPS; and the FY26 range genuinely is stated 'before any impact from prior-year self-insurance adjustments', so the apparent inconsistency the claim flags is a real inconsistency in ABM's own disclosure, not a misread. It is nonetheless the most priced item in the brief, for two reasons. First, publication: the Note 8 language, the definition change and the guidance footnote were all filed on 2026-06-05, and the CFO spent time on the Q2 call saying the change 'de-risked Q4' and gave 'greater predictability and transparency', while the Q2/Q4 actuarial-review cadence is repeated boilerplate across years of ABM 10-Ks and 10-Ks. Second and fatally, the claim's conclusion is the default modelling assumption rather than a deviation from it: nobody's Q3 estimate contains a prior-year reserve charge, so its absence is worth nothing. It also creates no year-over-year delta — Q3 FY25 adjusted net income of $51.7m (~$0.82/sh) was struck on the old, self-insurance-excluding basis, and the $1.04 consensus against 26.8% growth is being compared to exactly that $0.82, so the comp is already clean of this item on both sides. Arithmetically the claim proves that a $0.00 line stays $0.00.

findings.finding: Waterdrop's entire revenue growth story is one line: technical service income went RMB1.8m (Q4 2024) to RMB9.4m (Q1 2025) to RMB639.6m (Q4 2025) to RMB421.0m (Q1 2026) -- so it already fell 34.2% sequentially in Q1 2026 -- while brokerage income, the actual insurance business, was RMB648.6m / RMB670.8m / RMB724.8m over the same span, i.e. +11.7% YoY against the +64.8% headline, with sales and marketing rising from 22.9% to 43.6% of revenue and net profit falling to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m.
findings.adversary_note: Every component number is correct and every one of them is lifted from two press releases that went out on the full PR Newswire APAC wire and were carried by Morningstar, Yahoo, AOL, Manila Times, Macau Business, StockTitan and TipRanks. Technical service income RMB1.8m/9.4m/639.6m/421.0m checks out; insurance-related income 1,145.8 less 421.0 gives brokerage 724.8, and 658.0 less 9.4 gives 648.7, so +11.7% YoY is right; 1,310.4 less 639.6 gives 670.8; net profit RMB98.4m vs RMB108.2m is a line in the release. The only error is cosmetic: S&M was 43.5% of revenue, not 43.6%. What makes this priced is not the subtraction, which I could not find headlined anywhere, but the implication: TipRanks' 2026-06-16 note already said operating profit rose only 5.3% 'despite a sharp increase in sales and marketing spend'; management stated on the public Q1 call that 'operating profit scale is expected to remain broadly stable' in 2026 against roughly 40% revenue growth, which is them telling the market in advance that the revenue line is not flowing through; and the published estimate track already shows FY26 revenue revised UP from CN¥4.04b to CN¥4.56b while EPS was cut from CN¥1.46 to CN¥1.19 - the exact shape of this finding, already in the numbers people quote. Held at 70 rather than 85 only because the 'brokerage income +11.7%' figure itself is genuinely absent from all coverage I could find.

findings.finding: Huize Holding, the closest listed Chinese online life/health insurance brokerage, reported H1 2026 on 2026-08-20 with gross written premium +29.8% and first-year premium +48.7% but operating revenue up only 5.8% -- revenue per unit of premium fell from 21.1% to 17.2%, an 18.5% relative collapse in the channel take rate, in exactly the April-June window Waterdrop is about to report.
findings.adversary_note: The underlying data is entirely public and in wire copy: GlobeNewswire 2026-08-20, plus Yahoo, TipRanks, Quiver, Manila Times and a full Benzinga transcript. I reproduced the ratio - 719.8/4,196.4 = 17.15% against 680.5/3,233.7 = 21.05%, an 18.5% relative decline - so the arithmetic is right and the derivation is two divisions away from a press release. What holds this at 50 rather than higher is that nobody drew the ratio and nobody connected it to Waterdrop; the Huize coverage was uniformly positive ('Record Premiums and Profit Surge'), so the compression reading is not the told narrative. What holds it at 50 rather than lower is three factual objections to the claim as framed, which I state separately from pricing. First, 'exactly the April-June window' is wrong: this is a half-year report and you cannot isolate Q2 from it - half of the compression sits in Jan-Mar, a period Waterdrop has already reported. Second, revenue/GWP is not a take rate: GWP includes renewal premium that carries little incremental revenue, and Huize's FYP grew 48.7% into savings product where first-year commission is structurally far below long-term health protection, so a falling ratio is substantially a mix effect, not a rate cut. Third, the transmission channel to Waterdrop is weak by Waterdrop's own construction - 34% of its revenue is now technical service income, which is not premium commission at all.

findings.finding: Waterdrop will report Q2 2026 with no CFO (vacant since Kangping Shi left in June 2022), no head of finance (Xiaoying Xu resigned as VP of finance and head of finance effective 2026-07-31), and a replacement audit-committee financial expert who took the seat only on 2026-07-01 after Heping Feng resigned from the audit, compensation and nominating committees -- two finance-governance exits inside 30 days, both immediately after the FY2025 20-F carrying the undisclosed RMB639.6m revenue line.
findings.adversary_note: Both 'exits' are in wire copy with dated URLs and one of them has its own dedicated explainer article published a month before this print. The Feng resignation and the Qianfei Chang audit-chair appointment went out on PR Newswire on 2026-06-23 and were picked up by Nasdaq, TipRanks, Investing.com and Pluang the same day. The Xu resignation was 6-K'd on 2026-07-24, covered by TipRanks that day, and then written up at length by Simply Wall St and syndicated to Yahoo Finance on 2026-08-06 under the headline 'What Does Waterdrop's Finance Chief Exit Reveal About Its AI Investment Priorities?' - which is precisely this finding, published, thirty-two days before the print. The CFO vacancy dates to June 2022 and has been disclosed in four consecutive 20-Fs; age is not novelty. Separately, three of the claim's factual assertions do not survive checking. (i) 'No head of finance' is wrong or at least badly overstated: the very 6-K cited is signed by Jieru Li as 'Vice President of Finance, Board Secretary and Head of Strategy and Capital Markets', and the published coverage read her role as continuity in financial leadership. (ii) 'The FY2025 20-F carrying the undisclosed RMB639.6m revenue line' is wrong: RMB639.6m was disclosed by name in the Q4 2025 press release of 2026-03-25 and carried on the wire - and finding WDH#0 in this same brief correctly cites it as disclosed. (iii) Feng resigned as an independent director outright, not merely from three committees, and his replacement as audit chair was named in the same release on the same day, which is an orderly succession rather than a gap.

findings.finding: The US$50 million share repurchase authorisation expires on 2026-09-09 -- the day after this print -- with the great majority unused (cumulative buybacks moved only from US$118.1m to US$120.1m between the Q4 and Q1 releases, and the 20-F puts usage under the September 2025 programme at US$9.5m as of 2026-03-31), and Waterdrop has launched a new programme in September 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 and declared a US$0.03/ADS cash dividend alongside both its Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 results.
findings.adversary_note: The forward mechanical fact is real and I verified all of it - the $50m authorisation was approved 2025-09-02, announced on PR Newswire 2025-09-04, expressly runs 'during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026', cumulative repurchase ran $109.0m at 2025-08-31 to $120.1m at 2026-05-31 so roughly four-fifths is unused, and there have been five consecutive September programmes since 2021 with $0.03/ADS dividends attached to Q2 2025. But three things make it substantially priced. First, the expiry date is not obscure: it is stated in the company's own release and repeated in the FY2025 20-F, both a year old, and the 2026-08-06 Yahoo/Simply Wall St piece went into this print discussing the buyback and semiannual dividends as the capital-return frame. Second, five-for-five is a base rate, not news - this is 'structural and known', and the market has watched the identical announcement arrive on the Q2 print in each of 2024 and 2025. Third and most damaging, the flow is arguably already in the tape: the stock went $0.97 to $1.02 on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04, a 5.2% two-day move on a name with 0.83% daily vol and $255k of daily turnover, in the last two sessions before an authorisation with roughly $39m of unused capacity expires on 2026-09-09. That is exactly what company buying into an expiry looks like, and it is the baseline's entire +2.72% five-day run-up. So the mechanism reaches the print but part of it has already been paid for. Not higher than 60 because no one has written down 'expect a new authorisation on September 8', there is no option chain to express it, and no analyst to publish it.

findings.finding: WDH's NYSE Rule 802.01C 30-trading-day average closing price is $1.0263 as of 2026-09-04 (window 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-04), and the five sessions rolling out of that window closed $1.15/$1.15/$1.15/$1.14/$1.12, so the next five closes must average at least $0.984 to keep the average above $1.00 -- roughly 3.5% of cushion from the $1.02 spot, with the print the only scheduled catalyst inside that window.
findings.adversary_note: I reproduced the computation independently and every number is right, which is worth stating because it is unusual. The 30 trading sessions from 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-04 are exactly 30 (the summariser I used dropped 2026-08-24, a normal Monday session; Labor Day 2026 is 09-07, after the window). Summing the closes with 08-24 at $0.99 gives $30.79 and an average of $1.02633 - the claim's $1.0263 is correct to four decimals. The five sessions rolling out closed $1.15/$1.15/$1.15/$1.14/$1.12 for $5.71, leaving $25.08, so the next five closes must sum to $4.92, an average of $0.984, which is 3.5% below the $1.02 spot. I searched for an NYSE 802.01C notice and for any published version of this arithmetic and found neither, so the computation is genuinely not out - that is why this is not 70. What stops it being 15 is that the boundary itself is manifestly in the tape already: WDH closed at exactly $1.00 on thirteen consecutive sessions from 2026-08-05 through 2026-08-21, then $0.99 for five, then $0.97, then bounced to $1.02 immediately before the print. A three-week pin at precisely the listing threshold on a stock that turns $255k a day is not coincidence; the $1.00 line is being watched and defended, and the defence is the baseline's own run-up. Beyond that, the mechanism does not reach the horizon being measured and is directionally backwards from how such a finding usually reads: 802.01C produces a notice and a six-month cure period, not a delisting, and is routinely cured by an ADS ratio change; and a company with roughly $39m of unused repurchase authorisation expiring the day after the print has both the means and the motive to hold the line. The compliance boundary here is a floor argument, not a downside catalyst, and nothing about it resolves at the close after this print.

findings.finding: The EU 21st-package carve-out that drove DLNG from $3.32 (16 July) to $3.85 (23 July) is a third-country-deliveries-only derogation expiring 25 July 2027, renewable one year at a time by Council vote and capped at the operator's 2025 volumes; the AIS work identifying the Dynagas vessels it protects names Clean Planet, Clean Vision, Clean Ocean and Clean Horizon - none of which are among the listed partnership's six ships - while DLNG's own Yamal-chartered Lena River last called at Huelva, Spain, an EU import terminal, departing 25 August 2026, i.e. exactly the EU-delivery employment the derogation does not cover.
findings.adversary_note: The tape prices this twice, on the exact dates the information arrived, and has already round-tripped it. Confirmed closes: 15 Jul $3.65, 16 Jul $3.32 (-9% on the 21st-package LNG shipping ban threat), 22 Jul $3.69, 23 Jul $3.85 (+16% off the low on the Greek carve-out), 24 Jul $3.61 (-6.2%). Spot on 04 Sep is $3.66 - i.e. one cent above the pre-scare 15 July close. There is no residual carve-out premium left in the price to deflate, which is arithmetically fatal to the bearish inference regardless of whether the mechanism is right. On the mechanism itself: the third-country-deliveries-only limitation, the pre-24-Feb-2022 contract condition and the annual Council review were published in mainstream EU-policy press on 23 July 2026 - the very day of the rally peak - and in Steptoe/White & Case client alerts the same week; the stock then gave back 6.2% the next session. The 1 Jan 2027 EU restriction on the Yenisei River and Lena River Yamal charters is disclosed by the company itself in the 29 May 2026 Q1 6-K and the 8 Apr 2026 20-F, so the exposure is not news to anyone reading the issuer. Two factual notes. First, the finding's vessel-identity check is CORRECT and I verified it independently: the listed partnership's six hulls are Clean Energy, Ob River, Amur River, Arctic Aurora, Yenisei River and Lena River; Clean Planet and Clean Ocean sit under Dynagas Holding Ltd. and Clean Vision and Clean Horizon under Dynagas Equity Holding Ltd., i.e. the sponsor side, and urgewald's 18 Aug 2026 release does conflate them under 'Dynagas'. That is the highest-value unpublished element here and it is right. Second, the inference drawn from it is weak and arguably sign-reversed: the Article 3s-style derogation operates at the level of the EU (Greek) *operator* under pre-2022 contracts, not at the level of named hulls, so Dynagas Ltd's managed fleet - which includes DLNG's two Yamal ships - is inside it for third-country deliveries; and if only 2 of 6 listed hulls carry Yamal cargo against '5 of 14 Dynagas-linked Arc7' in the NGO framing, the honest read is that the NYSE entity carries *less* of the headline risk than the press release implies, which is a bull point, not a bear point. Third, the finding's renewal description is slightly wrong in the unhelpful direction: the derogation renews automatically for successive one-year periods unless the Council decides otherwise, it does not require an affirmative annual vote. Finally the Huelva datum is one voyage: Yamal Trade can and does redirect cargoes to third countries, and a legal August 2026 EU discharge says nothing about post-1-Jan-2027 routing. Channel is also poor - the 8 Sep release is a document plus a slide deck with no conference call, so there is no Q&A through which a sanctions re-framing can be forced into the price.

findings.finding: Clean Energy, the vessel DLNG moved onto a Rio Grande LNG charter 'at higher daily rates' at the end of April 2026, has sat at anchor in Southeast Asia in ballast (draught 8.9 m, speed 0.1 knots) with no destination and no ETA since departing Singapore Anchorage on 5 August 2026 - 33 days idle - while Arctic Aurora, still trading normally (loaded at Melkoya, Norway on 7 September for Klaipeda), is contracted to begin a second seven-year Rio Grande charter between September and November 2026, which would put a third of the six-ship fleet on hire to a project company whose Brownsville trains are not yet producing.
findings.adversary_note: The observation is real and I verified it from the same live page today (IMO 9323687 = CLEAN ENERGY, 2007-built, Marshall Islands; at anchor, South East Asia, 0.1 knots, draught 8.9 m against a 12.4 m laden draught, no destination, no ETA, last port Singapore Anch. 1 departed 5 August 06:58 UTC). I found no financial-media coverage of it, so the fact itself is close to unpublished. But two of the finding's three legs are old wire copy and the third is mis-specified. The Arctic Aurora seven-year Rio Grande charter commencing September-November 2026 and the Clean Energy two-year charter commencing March-May 2026 were both announced on 18 July 2023 and are restated in every 20-F since; 'a third of the fleet on hire to Rio Grande' has therefore been a published fact for three years. That Rio Grande's Brownsville trains are not producing is equally public - NextDecade's own 2026 business updates guide first gas H2 2026 and first LNG from Train 1 in H1 2027 - and it was never a surprise, because the 2023 charters were deliberately struck to start ahead of the plant. The mis-specification is the one that matters: these are time charters, so hire runs whether the charterer trades the ship or parks her, and a vessel idled at the charterer's direction is on-hire, not off-hire. The finding therefore does not demonstrate lost revenue; it demonstrates that Rio Grande LNG is paying for a steam-turbine carrier it has no cargo for, which is a counterparty-credit observation about NextDecade, not a DLNG revenue observation. And the timing kills the mechanism: the idling began 5 August 2026, which is Q3. The 8 September release covers the quarter ended 30 June, so this cannot appear in the reported numbers, and with no conference call there is no forum in which it can be raised. What genuinely does sit inside the Q2 window - roughly four weeks of Clean Energy off-hire between SEFE redelivery in early April and Rio Grande delivery at end-April - was already disclosed in the 29 May 2026 Q1 release. I also note a source conflict I cannot resolve: a MarineTraffic crawl surfaced in search shows the same IMO underway off the Indian coast at 13.2 knots, so the AIS aggregators disagree, and the reading is un-archivable and may have changed since it was taken.

findings.finding: Six directors of Dynagas LNG Partners filed initial Section 16 ownership statements on 18 and 30 March 2026, every one of them carrying event date 18 March 2026 - George Prokopiou reporting 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd (50.4% beneficial interest), Alexios Rodopoulos 500 units direct, Dimitrios Anagnostopoulos 'no securities owned' - even though the partnership is exempt from Section 16 as a foreign private issuer under Rule 3a12-3(b), filed a 20-F for FY2025 on 8 April 2026 and has continued filing 6-Ks rather than 10-Qs through 13 August 2026; no Form 4 has followed in the five and a half months since.
findings.adversary_note: Every factual element checks out - I confirmed one Form 3 filed 2026-03-18 and five filed 2026-03-30, all with event date 18 March 2026; the Prokopiou form reports 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units held indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd. with a 50.4% interest and the usual disclaimer; the FY2025 20-F was filed 2026-04-08 and 6-Ks have continued through 2026-08-13. So the finding is not wrong about anything. It is, however, split between a substantive part that is 95% priced and an anomaly with no demonstrated mechanism. The substance - Prokopiou/Dynagas Holding controlling 15,595,000 common units and the GP - has been in every 20-F and in the 2013 424B4 for a decade; there is nothing new in the number, and the Form 3s report no transaction, so they are not insider buying or selling and carry no directional content at all. The anomaly - an issuer exempt from Section 16 under Rule 3a12-3(b) filing Form 3s anyway - is genuinely obscure and I found zero media coverage of it. But the finding itself supplies the disconfirming evidence: five and a half months later there is no Form 4, no 10-Q, no transition to domestic-filer status and no Schedule 13E-3, and the issuer has kept filing on the foreign-private-issuer track. Absent any follow-through, a filing-agent artefact or a belt-and-braces precaution is a better explanation than a corporate event, and I searched for a take-private or merger proposal and found none. The documents are also on EDGAR full-text search and have been for nearly six months, so 'nobody wrote about it' is not the same as 'nobody could see it'. As for reaching the print: a Q2 earnings release cannot resolve a Section 16 filing-status question, and there is no call. The one live piece of corporate action here - the $10m unit repurchase programme running to 24 November 2026 - was announced 10 December 2025 and is fully public.

findings.finding: UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide implies Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $156-176mm, but the company itself quantified the prior-year Q4 as depressed by $40-50mm of cyber-incident adjusted EBITDA, so on a cyber-clean basis Q4 FY26 EBITDA is roughly flat to +13% (mid ~+3%) against reported growth of +34% to +52%, and against +23.4% in Q2 and +16.6% in Q3 — the underlying run-rate that has to support a ~$745-760mm FY27 guide on the way to the $800mm FY28 Investor Day target has decelerated to near zero.
findings.adversary_note: The arithmetic is correct in every particular — I verified it independently. FY26 guide is adj EBITDA $685-705mm (Q3 FY26 release, 2026-06-09), 39-week actual is $529mm, so the implied Q4 is exactly $156-176mm; Q4 FY25 adj EBITDA was $116mm and the company said the cyberattack cut it by 'approximately $50 million' in that same quarter. So the claim is right, and it is right entirely out of two documents the company published and the trade press headlined. Modern Distribution Management ran the headline 'UNFI Says Cyberattack Cost is up to $400M in Sales, $50M in EBITDA' on the FY25 Q4 print. The easy-comp structure is already in consensus: Zacks has Q4 EPS at $0.62 against a prior-year loss of $0.11 — the street is modelling the swing off the cyber-depressed base, which is only possible if it has already re-based the comparison. The FY28 $800mm target and the 'low-double-digit average annual adjusted EBITDA growth FY25-FY28' framing the claim leans on were published at the December 2025 Investor Day. This is a re-statement of published guidance plus a subtraction the sell-side cannot avoid doing, which is the 90-100 anchor softened only by the fact that nobody has written the 'underlying is zero, so FY27 is at risk' sentence out loud in preview copy. If anything the claim understates itself — using the confirmed $50mm rather than the $40-50mm estimate range, cyber-clean Q4 growth is -6% to +6%, midpoint zero, not +3%.

findings.finding: SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026 (-13%, faster than CBO projected, with Arizona -55%, Florida -22%), and this data was published on 2026-08-21 — after UNFI last guided on 2026-06-09; UNFI's Conventional ($3.136bn) plus Retail ($515mm) segments were ~47% of Q3 FY26 net sales and are precisely the SNAP-exposed channels.
findings.adversary_note: Every figure checks out against the PBS piece (42.2m May-2025, 36.6m May-2026, >13%, Arizona -55% April-to-April, Florida -22%, CBO's 2030 level reached in 2026) — but that piece is an AP wire story that ran on PBS, ABC News, NBC Washington, KSAT, Newser, Yahoo and Food Manufacturing on 2026-08-21, and Grocery Dive published a dedicated state-by-state SNAP-participation piece for the grocery-industry audience. This is national wire copy, not an obscure dataset. More damaging: UNFI's own CEO said on the 2026-06-09 call that 'the reduction in SNAP funding is beginning to make an impact or continuing to make an impact,' so the company has already told the market the headwind exists and has already embedded its view of it in the guide. The unpublished increment is only the elasticity — nobody has multiplied 47%-of-sales by a SNAP-dollar decline. That increment is real but modest: SNAP is roughly 8-9% of US grocery dollars, a 13% enrollment fall is maybe a 1% headwind to the exposed channel, and UNFI is a wholesaler whose Conventional volume is one step removed and largely pass-through.

findings.finding: Both listed natural-channel retailers reported negative traffic inside UNFI's Q4 window (2026-05-03 to 2026-08-01): Natural Grocers' quarter ended 2026-06-30 showed daily-average comps +1.2% built entirely on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin down 60bp, and Sprouts' June quarter showed comps -1% with management citing weaker June trends — while UNFI's Natural segment (+4.4% in Q3) is the only growing part of the company and the pillar of the FY27 return-to-growth guide.
findings.adversary_note: Both legs verify: NGVC daily-average comps +1.2% on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin 29.9%→29.3%, and Sprouts Q2 comps -1.0%. But Sprouts is a $6bn+ company whose comp print on 2026-07-30 was covered by Grocery Dive, Supermarket News, TipRanks, Shelby Report and every wire, and 'natural-channel demand is cooling / traffic is negative' is one of the most widely told grocery narratives of 2026. That is the definition of a story already in the sector's price. The claim is also selectively read: NGVC's comp *accelerated* from +0.5% in Q2 to +1.2% in Q3, and Sprouts still grew sales 5% and beat on EPS — the release attributes the comp decline to lapping a prior-year produce surge, not to demand collapse. Negative transaction count with positive basket is the standard 2026 grocery signature and is not specific to the natural channel. And this is the same underlying document as UNFI-b#1: one NGVC release, cited twice from two URLs.

findings.finding: Amazon's physical-stores net sales — the reported line for Whole Foods, UNFI's largest customer at roughly a quarter of net sales — were $5,794mm in the June-2026 quarter versus $5,595mm a year earlier, +4% and +4% excluding FX, essentially unchanged from the +4.6% March-quarter pace, covering two-thirds of UNFI's Q4.
findings.adversary_note: I verified the numbers exactly against the Amazon exhibit: physical stores $5,794m vs $5,595m, '4%' and '4%' ex-FX, with the March-2026 quarter at $5,785m. The claim is factually clean. It is also lifted verbatim from the single most-read earnings document of the quarter, published 2026-07-30 and parsed line-by-line by thousands of analysts within minutes, and the Whole Foods concentration it depends on is a standing disclosure in UNFI's 10-K. The information content is close to nil in any case: the finding says the largest customer's growth is *unchanged*, which is the null hypothesis. A datapoint whose content is 'no change' cannot be a mispricing however obscure the read-across; and physical stores is Amazon's Whole Foods plus Fresh plus Go, so it is a noisy proxy that does not isolate UNFI's actual customer.

findings.finding: UNFI pulled its Q4/full-year report forward roughly three weeks against a stable four-year pattern — 2026-09-08 versus 2025-09-30, 2024-10-01 and late September in the two prior years — and announced the new date on 2026-08-10, the exact day the incoming CFO started, five and a half weeks after a 1 August fiscal year end.
findings.adversary_note: The pull-forward is real and I confirmed the prior pattern: FY24 Q4 reported 2024-10-01 and FY25 Q4 reported 2025-09-30, against 2026-09-08 for a fiscal year ended 2026-08-01 — 38 days versus roughly 59. But the fact itself is not obscure at all: it went out on Business Wire on 2026-08-10 and was carried by Yahoo Finance, StockTitan, Zacks and the earnings calendars, and it is the single date every holder of this option chain is trading around. What is unpublished is only the inference, and the inference is weak in both directions and arguably backwards: 38 days is exactly the lag UNFI already runs on Q1-Q3 (Q3 ended 2026-05-02, reported 2026-06-09 — 38 days), so the change normalises Q4 onto the existing cadence rather than creating an anomaly. The baseline's own plausibility check reads 'fits_cadence, 91 days against a 91-day cadence.' Scheduling signal is also sign-ambiguous — the literature cuts toward early reporters having good news, so a hunter using this as a warning is arguing against its own prior.

findings.finding: The initial FY27 guide — the single largest swing factor in this print — will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10, four weeks before, as part of four senior changes in seven weeks around the fiscal year end: Matteo Tarditi moved off CFO to President/COO, Alfredo Luchini arrived as CFO from Carrier, supply-chain head Mark Bushway was announced as departing 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased in the role on 2026-08-24.
findings.adversary_note: All four items sit in a single press release that UNFI issued and filed as exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K on 2026-07-09 — I read it: Tarditi to President/COO, Luchini from Carrier as CFO effective 2026-08-10, Bushway departing 2027-01-01. Not a discovery in a footnote; a company-issued announcement, wire-distributed, and picked up in the August trade and financial press summaries of UNFI leadership. 'A CFO four weeks in the seat sets the first multi-year guide' is a real and reasonable risk, but it is a heuristic every buy-side desk applies automatically the moment a CFO change is announced eight weeks before a guide date — that is the textbook definition of structural-and-known. The Echols item is immaterial: a Chief Corporate Affairs Officer does not touch the EBITDA guide. UNFI-b#2 is the same document and the same thesis; this should not be counted twice.

findings.finding: UNFI's fuel hedge book is a $5m Level-2 current asset as of 2026-05-02 (up from $1m at 2026-01-31) - trivially small against a $1.87/gal year-over-year diesel move - and being entirely current it expires inside FY27, exactly the year whose guide is set on 8 September, with US on-highway diesel at $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 (+$1.865 YoY) after having fallen to $4.578 on 2026-07-06.
findings.adversary_note: The diesel facts are exact — $5.599/gal for the week of 2026-08-31 and $4.578 on 2026-07-06 both verify — but that is the problem: US on-highway diesel rose 53.8% from early January to early August 2026, the largest January-to-August move in 32 years of weekly EIA data, driven by Strait of Hormuz disruption and Russia's export ban. This is front-page macro that has repriced every freight-intensive equity in the market, and the read-across from diesel to a private-fleet food distributor is the most obvious one there is. Worse for the claim, UNFI already told the market its position on 2026-06-09: fuel and transportation pressure is 'embedded' in Q4 guidance, and management named three mitigants — 'we hedge part of the fuel,' contractual protection (i.e. surcharges), and route optimisation. The genuinely unpublished increment is the $5m Level-2 balance from an XBRL R-page, and that increment carries a logical flaw: a $5m mark-to-market fair value tells you nothing about notional hedged volume, and in a violently rising diesel market a small positive MTM is as consistent with a decent hedge that has already been marked as with no hedge at all. The claim infers size from fair value. Third-party corroboration also cuts against novelty: Natural Grocers named 'higher freight costs' as a gross-margin driver in its 2026-08-06 release, so the freight-cost transmission is already visible in published documents.

findings.finding: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, which buys 69% of its product from UNFI, reported its quarter ended 2026-06-30 - sitting entirely inside UNFI's Q4 - with net sales up only 1.8%, daily average transaction COUNT down 1.8%, gross margin down 60bp on unfavourable mix and higher freight, and cut the top end of both its FY26 EPS guide ($2.15 to $2.11) and its comp guide (2.5% to 2.0%), all against a prior-year base that its own release says was distorted by the cybersecurity incident at its primary distributor.
findings.adversary_note: This is the same document as UNFI-a#2 — the NGVC Q3 FY26 release of 2026-08-06 — read from the SEC exhibit instead of the IR page. Every number verifies (net sales +1.8% to $334.7m, transaction count -1.8%, gross margin 29.9%→29.3% on mix, shrink and freight, FY26 EPS guide $2.07-2.15→$2.07-2.11, comps 1.5-2.5%→1.5-2.0%) and the primary-distributor cyber distortion is in the release, along with a $2.0m business-interruption insurance gain. Two things blunt it. First, one factual error: the claim says NGVC's quarter sits 'entirely inside UNFI's Q4' — it does not. NGVC's quarter is 1 April to 30 June 2026; UNFI's Q4 is 3 May to 1 August. April falls in UNFI's Q3 and July is missing entirely, so the overlap is two of three months. Second, the magnitude: NGVC's total net sales are ~$1.3bn annualised, of which ~69% bought from UNFI is roughly $0.9bn, under 3% of UNFI's ~$31bn. A top-end-only guide trim at a customer worth 3% of revenue is not a print-moving fact on its own, and the 69% dependency has been an annual 10-K disclosure for years — age is not novelty. What survives is the channel read-across, and that is a shared story with the far more visible Sprouts print.

findings.finding: Five senior officer changes between 2026-07-09 and 2026-08-24 - CFO Matteo Tarditi moved to President/COO, Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, external hire Alfredo Luchini (ex-Carrier) became CFO on 2026-08-10, Chief Supply Chain Officer Mark Bushway exits 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased to serve on 2026-08-24 - so a CFO four weeks into the seat delivers UNFI's first multi-year guide, and the Echols departure was disclosed only in an exit Form 4 with no 8-K and no press release.
findings.adversary_note: Four of the five changes are in one company-issued press release filed as exhibit 99.1 on 2026-07-09 — Tarditi, Martin, Luchini and Bushway are all named in it, which I confirmed by reading it — and the August financial press recapped the same slate. So the 'five changes in seven weeks' framing overstates the discovery: it is one announcement plus one Form 4. The genuine increment is the Echols exit disclosed only via a 2026-08-24 Form 4 with no 8-K, which is a legitimately obscure catch, and it is also the least material of the five: Chief Corporate Affairs Officer sits nowhere near the FY27 EBITDA guide, and a departure with no 8-K is consistent with the company's own view that it is not material — correctly, under Item 5.02, which only compels disclosure for named executive officers. This is the same document and the same thesis as UNFI-a#5 and should not be scored as two independent findings; the marginal information over a#5 is small, which is why this sits slightly lower rather than materially lower.

findings.finding: Canaan's self-mining run-rate halved entering Q3 while it reported installed hashrate as flat: monthly BTC produced went 90 (April) / 90 (May) / 64 (June) / 46 (July) = 3.00 / 2.90 / 2.13 / 1.48 BTC per day, a 51% per-day decline, driven by Ethiopia (4.96 EH/s, a third of the 14.9 EH/s installed fleet) falling from 2.33 EH/s operating at 30 April to 0.36 EH/s at 30 June and then being described as 'paused' at 31 July -- yet the July release counted the entire paused 4.96 EH/s inside its headline 'operating computing power' of 14.24 EH/s, one month after the same table had shown Ethiopia at 0.36 EH/s operating.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is a company press release and the central inference was published two days after the filing. The Block ran the production decline as wire copy on the filing date itself (2026-08-17, 'Bitcoin production slips again in July for CleanSpark, BitFuFu and Canaan', naming Canaan as the worst of the three at -28% to 46 BTC), and CryptoSlate on 2026-08-19 drew out precisely the hunter's core point in its headline -- that the paused Ethiopia 4.96 EH/s is ~35% of the 14.24 EH/s July 'operating' total -- and even made the June 0.36 vs July 4.96 comparison the hunter treats as the discovery. The filing verifies out (I confirmed 46 BTC, Ethiopia 4.96/4.96 with 'Canaan has paused its mining operations in Ethiopia, but its hashrate remains part of the Company's installed hashrate'), and it is in fact WORSE than stated: group operating power was 7.45 EH/s in the June release and 14.24 EH/s in the July one, so the whole operating column appears to have been backfilled with installed values. But the residual novelty is arithmetic on published monthlies, not a new fact. And the reach into a 30-June print is limited: Q2 self-mined output (90 April + 90 May + 64 June = 244 BTC) was pre-disclosed month by month, so the mining revenue line is effectively already public; the 46-BTC July collapse and any Ethiopia impairment land in Q3, and the June outage began only 'in mid-June' per the company. The -0.43% reaction on 2026-08-17 is a market that read the release and shrugged.

findings.finding: Canaan converted its automatic shelf into a $270m standard Form F-3 on 15 April 2026 specifically because it 'expects that it will cease to be a well-known seasoned issuer' on filing its FY2025 20-F, then filed Post-Effective Amendment No. 5 on 15 June 2026 as an 'exhibits-only filing to file an updated auditor consent' -- i.e. it is actively keeping a shelf equal to roughly its entire market value usable -- against cash that fell from US$80.8m at 31 December 2025 to US$43.5m at 31 March 2026, a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m, US$21.1m short-term debt, and zero 424B5 takedowns anywhere in 2026 after three in 2025 (March, October, November).
findings.adversary_note: Every component checks out against primary documents -- I verified the 2026-04-15 POSASR (Post-Effective Amendment No. 1 to Reg. No. 333-285125, $270,000,000 on the fee table, with the explanatory note that 'the Registrant expects that it will cease to be a well-known seasoned issuer ... upon filing its Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025'), the 2026-06-15 exhibits-only auditor-consent POSAM No. 5, the Q1 cash walk of $80.8m to $43.5m, the $22.9m Q1 gross loss and the $21.1m short-term debt, and the complete absence of any 424B5 in 2026 after 2025-03-07, 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-04. This is the cleanest finding in the brief on facts. It is also the least published: the $270m shelf appears only as an automated filing summary on StockTitan (2026-04-28), framed there as 'a routine capital-raising mechanism', and the WKSI-loss motive and the shelf-to-market-cap ratio (~$270m against ~$249m of ADSs at $0.36) appear nowhere I could find. Against that: the balance-sheet stress itself is thoroughly priced -- the Q1 release carrying the cash collapse and the gross loss printed -13.66% on 2026-05-19, the largest move in the baseline and, notably, the one row in that untrustworthy history that IS a real earnings reaction. And the claim materially understates the mitigant: Canaan told the market on 2026-08-04 that it holds ~US$130m of digital assets and that 'our operations continue to generate bitcoin, providing us with a flexible source of capital', which is the company pre-announcing that it will sell BTC rather than hit the shelf. Dry powder plus motive is not a catalyst; the catalyst would be a takedown, and there has not been one in ten months at prices far above today's.

findings.finding: There is a mid-June 2026 open-market insider buy cluster that is essentially invisible for this name because Canaan is a 20-F/6-K filer whose officers nonetheless file Section 16 forms: CFO Cheng Jin bought 65,000 ADSs at US$0.35 on 15 June, and CEO Nangeng Zhang bought 250,000 ADSs at US$0.34 on 17 June and 250,000 at US$0.33 on 18 June, and no insider has filed any transaction since 22 June -- no sales at all into the 68% rally.
findings.adversary_note: The premise is factually false and that is the whole verdict. This cluster is not 'essentially invisible' -- Canaan issued a dedicated press release about it on PR Newswire on 2026-06-24 headlined 'Canaan Inc. Announces Open Market Share Purchases by Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer', disclosing that 'Zhang and Cheng together acquired a total of 1,065,000 American Depositary Shares of the Company at an average price of US$0.35 per ADS', with CEO commentary about conviction in the strategy. It was carried by Morningstar and written up by TipRanks ('Canaan Executives Buy Over 1 Million ADSs in Open-Market Purchases'). The stock fell 5.87% on the day of that release. Worse for the claim, the enumeration is incomplete: the three transactions listed total 565,000 ADSs, but Form 4 accession 0001802993-26-000003 (filed 2026-06-17) shows Zhang also bought 250,000 at $0.35 on 15 June and 250,000 at $0.35 on 16 June, so the real cluster is 1,065,000 ADSs -- exactly what the company said. The residual -- no insider filings since 22 June, no sales into the rally -- is an absence of EDGAR entries anyone can see in thirty seconds, and in dollars the whole cluster is ~$373k against a ~$249m market cap, 0.15%. Signal value only, and the signal was broadcast.

findings.finding: Canaan is inside its second and final Nasdaq minimum-bid-price compliance period, expiring 11 January 2027, with the ADSs at US$0.36 -- needing roughly +178% and then ten consecutive closes at or above US$1.00 -- and the company has committed to nothing more than that it 'will evaluate all available options during the second compliance period to rectify the deficiency'; I found no depositary notice of any Canaan reverse split or ADS-ratio change, and an ADS-ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A shares) needs no shareholder vote and can be effected in weeks.
findings.adversary_note: The compliance facts are in the wire copy verbatim. Canaan press-released the second 180-day extension to 11 January 2027 on PR Newswire on 2026-07-15, including the exact sentence the hunter quotes about evaluating 'all available options during the second compliance period', and it was covered by Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, Blockspace and StockTitan the same day. The claim's own quotation of the company language is the tell: it is quoting a public press release. What is left is mechanism commentary -- that an ADS-ratio change needs no shareholder vote and can be effected in weeks, and that no depositary notice has appeared -- which is true, structural, and known to anyone who has watched a sub-$1 ADS before. Age is not novelty here: Canaan has been non-compliant through an entire first 180-day period. Crucially it does not reach this print. Nothing in a 30-June results release resolves a January 2027 bid-price deadline, the deadline is four months out, and the market's reaction on the day the extension was granted was +0.69% -- a shrug, because an extension is the benign outcome.

findings.finding: Cipher Mining's 53,762,660 CAN ADSs (806,439,900 Class A shares, ~9.2% of the 585.8m reported float), issued to it at US$0.7394/ADS on 2026-02-23 as payment for the ABC Projects JV stake, came out of lock-up on 2026-08-23 -- Cipher's own 10-Q states the date and carries the position inside 'Prepaid expenses and other current assets', and the shares were never registered for resale, so Cipher can sell under Rule 144 as a non-affiliate with no volume cap and no Form 144 trail.
findings.adversary_note: The lock-up was disclosed by Canaan itself in the deal announcement seven months ago and every number in the claim has been in print since February. Canaan's 2026-02-24 press release states the consideration was 'the issuance of 806,439,900 Canaan Inc. Class A ordinary shares to Cipher, equivalent to 53,762,660 American Depositary Shares ("ADS"), priced at US$0.7394 per ADS and subject to a lock-up period of six months' -- the ADS count, the price and the six-month term, all of it -- and it was carried by CoinDesk, The Block, Nasdaq, PR Newswire, Blockspace and DCD. Cipher's own 10-Q, which the hunter cites, restates the lock-up and its expiry, and Cipher's Q1 10-Q filed in May carried the same disclosure. More decisively, the event has already happened: the lock-up expired 2026-08-23 and the stock rose through it, +16% on 2026-08-25 into Bitcoin Asia, on ~23.5m ADS a day. Two full weeks of free-float have already traded post-expiry. And a lock-up expiry is not a thing a results release discloses or changes -- the mechanism has no route into the 8 September print at all.

findings.finding: The 2026-08-04 'repurchase shares using digital asset treasury' release that lit the +68% run adds no new authorisation and no dollar figure -- it points back to a US$30m board authorisation dated 2025-12-12 that expires 2026-12-12 and that Canaan's own Q1 release says had bought only ~2.8m ADSs for ~US$2.0m (6.7%), after the prior US$30m programme executed just US$4.9m (16%); the Sept 8 release is the first document that must state repurchases through 30 June.
findings.adversary_note: The 'no new authorisation' point is in the plain text of the release it debunks. The 2026-08-04 exhibit says repurchases will occur 'under the Company's existing share repurchase authorization' effective 12 December 2025, gives no dollar figure, and PR Newswire and Globe-and-Mail coverage of it said the same -- the announcement 'did not authorize a new repurchase amount'. The execution history is public too: the Q1 release of 2026-05-19 disclosed ~2.8m ADSs for ~US$2.0m under the current programme, and the 2025-12-17 6-K disclosed that the prior US$30m programme from 27 May 2025 had bought 6,586,413 ADSs for ~US$4.9m, which MarketScreener and Investing.com both wrote up. So the arithmetic the claim performs (6.7% and 16% execution) is arithmetic on published figures, not a discovery. The causal framing is also wrong in a way that damages the thesis: the 2026-08-04 release produced +12.43% on the day and then faded -- spot was ~$0.214 around 2026-08-06 and only $0.2712 on 2026-08-20 -- and the +68% run was lit by the CLARITY Act push on 2026-08-20 (+12.95%) and Bitcoin Asia on 2026-08-25 (+16%), not by the buyback release. There is therefore little buyback premium left to deflate. Finally the claim's own catalyst is self-defeating: repurchases 'through 30 June' predate the 4 August announcement entirely, so the Q2 number can barely differ from the $2.0m already disclosed on 19 May and tells you nothing about whether the BTC-funded buying has actually happened. What is genuinely unpriced is thin: that a US$30m authorisation is 12% of market cap and this management has executed 6.7% of it, which is a credibility point rather than a numbers point.

findings.finding: The Q4 FY2026 revenue guide of US$23-26m given on 2026-06-08 implies a year-over-year decline of -15.0% to -24.8%, two to three times the -7.5%/-7.8%/-9.1% printed in Q1/Q2/Q3, because Q4 FY2025 revenue was US$30.6m -- a figure the company has never reported and that only exists as FY2025 US$118.0m minus nine-month FY2025 US$87,390,942.
findings.adversary_note: The load-bearing novelty premise is factually FALSE, and I can quote the refutation twice. The claim says Q4 FY2025 revenue is 'a figure the company has never reported and that only exists as FY2025 US$118.0m minus nine-month FY2025 US$87,390,942.' The company reported it verbatim on 2025-09-09, in a PR Newswire release furnished on EDGAR as ex99-1 to 6-K 0001493152-25-012895, under section headers 'Fourth Quarter of Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Highlights' and 'Fourth Quarter of Fiscal Year 2025 Unaudited Financial Results': 'Total revenue was US$30.7 million, representing a 2.9% decrease from US$31.6 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024.' Gamehaus reports every standalone quarter with a call and a transcript; nothing here requires cross-document subtraction. On top of that, the US$23-26m Q4 guide is published guidance given 2026-06-08 and carried by PR Newswire, TradingView, Manila Times, StockTitan, Benzinga, Globe and Mail, thestockobserver, scanx and grafa. Both operands of the YoY division are in wire copy; the division is one keystroke. Separately, the derived base is slightly wrong: using the reported 30.7 the range is -15.3% to -25.1%, not -15.0% to -24.8%. And the magnitude read is one-sided: the company printed at or above the TOP of its guide in Q2 (26.3 vs 24-27) and Q3 (26.2 vs 24-26), so a 26.0 print gives -15%, i.e. 1.6x the prior decline rate, not 3x; meanwhile net income rose YoY for three straight quarters (+17.6%, +151.2%, +16.4%) on a 10.1% opex cut, which is the framing the wires actually used ('Q3 revenue exceeds guidance as margins expand'). The one genuinely unwritten piece is that the guide breaks Q4 seasonality (Q4 FY2025 was +6.6% sequential; the guide implies -12% to -1%). That is worth something, but not much on a name where the guide itself is a month old and public.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-12 the company said it will 'progressively optimize its third-party publishing business in casual titles, and in particular in the social casino category' and is now running its existing portfolio 'with user acquisition and operating expenditure allocated according to return on investment rather than scale' effective the current quarter -- and that release traded 22,679 shares, under 6% of the baseline's 408,260 twenty-day average, closing $0.79 to $0.74 to $0.70.
findings.adversary_note: Every quoted word is verbatim from a PR Newswire release dated 2026-08-12 and is therefore in the wire copy 27 days before the print. It was syndicated to AOL and headlined by StockTitan as 'Gamehaus Shifts Strategy to AI Content Tools.' The claim's own tape evidence also cuts against it in a way the claim does not report: yes, only 22,908 shares traded on 2026-08-12 and the stock went $0.79 to $0.74 to $0.70 (-11.4%, and I confirm those closes exactly) — but on 2026-08-14 it printed +7.66% to $0.76 on 142,571 shares, six times the release-day volume, so two-thirds of the markdown was reversed within one session on higher volume. The market saw it, marked it down, and un-marked it. The residual edge is genuinely there and is why this is not an 80: the release quantifies nothing, and the Sep 8 call will attach a Q1 FY2027 revenue guide to a deliberate wind-down of the revenue base — and social casino is unambiguously the base (three of the five apps in GAMEHAUS PTE. LTD's Apple account are Bingo Island, Vegas Party Casino Slots and Double Win Slots; the top Google Play titles are Double Rich Casino Slots and Lucky Hit Classic Casino Slots). A first quantification of a self-inflicted revenue decline is new. The strategy statement is not.

findings.finding: The baseline's +11.95% five-day run-up is almost entirely one session -- 2026-08-31, 7,314,944 shares (about 27% of the 27,038,542 non-affiliate shares the F-3 counts) and +16.51% to $0.85 -- reacting to a 6-K filed 2026-08-28 that merely extended a US$5m buyback of which only ~US$600,000 (518,063 shares) had been used in twelve months; the identical event a year earlier produced +103.54% on ~46m shares and fully retraced.
findings.adversary_note: This is a claim about the price rather than about the company, so almost by construction it is in the price. Every element is either on EDGAR or on the public tape: I confirm 2026-08-31 close $0.85, +16.51%, volume 7,314,944 (stockanalysis.com), and I confirm the 6-K of 2026-08-28 states the program was extended to 2027-08-28 with 'approximately 518,063 Class A Ordinary Shares for approximately US$600,000' repurchased. I also confirm the 5-day run-up is arithmetically that one session: 2026-08-28 $0.73 to 2026-09-04 $0.82. And the fade is already visible without waiting for the print — $0.85, $0.84, $0.82, $0.79, $0.82 across 08-31 to 09-04, i.e. the market gave back a quarter of the spike in three sessions on its own. The precedent is also published: the original US$5m authorisation was press-released on 2025-08-28 and Investing.com reported the stock 'soars', with the surge widely put at ~93%. The one thing the claim adds that is not written anywhere is the reading that a 6-K-only extension of a program 12% used is not information — but that reading is a baseline correction, not an edge, and the correction is one the tape has already begun making.

findings.finding: The FY2027 growth premise management gave on 2026-06-08 -- 'the user base to return to growth as multiple new titles launch through fiscal 2027', with one RPG live by end of Q2 calendar 2026, one 'launching around September' and one signed for an August-to-September launch -- has no visible trace: neither Apple developer account (GAMEHAUS PTE. LTD, 5 apps; GAMEHAUS LIMITED, 4 apps) lists a single RPG title, and the Aug 12 strategy release does not mention the RPG pipeline at all.
findings.adversary_note: The promise half is fully published and I verified it verbatim in three places (Globe and Mail, Benzinga transcript, thestockobserver, all 2026-06-08): one RPG in commercial testing for end-Q2-calendar-2026 in Hong Kong/Macau/Taiwan, a second custom-developed RPG 'on track for launch around September', a third signed for an August-to-September window, and 'the user base to return to growth as multiple new titles launch through fiscal 2027'. The absence half is not published anywhere and I confirm the observation as far as it goes: GAMEHAUS PTE. LTD's Apple developer page lists exactly five apps — North Tower! Merge TD Defense, Match Tile Scenery, Bingo Island, Vegas Party Casino Slots, Double Win Slots — and not one is an RPG. But the negative evidence is methodologically weak in three ways the claim does not address. Gamehaus is a publisher of third-party titles, so an RPG 'signed for global distribution' plausibly ships under the developer's own Apple account. The first RPG was explicitly to launch 'initially in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan', which are separate App Store storefronts that a US-storefront developer page does not enumerate. And Apple developer pages do not reliably surface soft-launched or region-limited titles. So this is absence of evidence in the one place where evidence would least be expected. Worse for its independence: the reason the Aug 12 release does not mention the RPG pipeline is that the Aug 12 release announces a different strategy — which is GMHS#1. The two claims are one fact seen from two sides.

findings.finding: A dilution and entrenchment sequence executed in five weeks and never described anywhere as a sequence: Class B voting power raised from 15 to 50 votes per share by shareholder vote on 2026-07-10 (15,598,113 Class B shares, so ~95% of votes), a US$200,000,000 primary Form F-3 shelf filed 2026-07-28 stating a non-affiliate float of US$23,523,531.54, that shelf going EFFECT 2026-08-11/12 -- the same window as the AI narrative release -- and no 424B on file as of 2026-09-07, meaning the ~US$7.8m baby-shelf capacity (one third of float) is entirely unused and live.
findings.adversary_note: Every component is on EDGAR, and I verified each one verbatim. The Class B increase from fifteen to fifty votes was approved 2026-07-10 and reported in the 6-K filed 2026-07-14 (27,765,163 for, 20,686 against at the Class A meeting), and it is then restated in the F-3 prospectus itself: 'each Class B Ordinary Share carries fifty (50) votes'. The F-3 of 2026-07-28 registers 'up to US$200,000,000' and states on its cover 'US$23,523,531.54 based on the closing price of US$0.87 per Class A Ordinary Share on July 27, 2026 and 27,038,542 Class A Ordinary Shares held by non-affiliates' — the claim's figures are exact. The F-3 itself discloses the I.B.5 baby-shelf constraint and that no securities were sold under it in the prior twelve months, so the ~US$7.8m unused capacity is disclosed by the company, not discovered. StockTitan indexed the EFFECT notice on 2026-08-12 for retail. What is left is the 'sequence' framing, and the entrenchment leg of it is economically null: with 15,598,113 Class B at fifteen votes against 37,971,245 Class A (FY2025 20-F), insiders already controlled ~86% of the vote. Going to ~95% moves nobody from minority to control; it changes nothing about who decides anything, and it transfers no value on its own. The dilution leg is real — US$7.8m against a ~US$45-53m cap is ~15-17% potential dilution and is large against US$18.3m of cash — but it is capacity, not a deal, and it does not resolve on Sep 8. A raise after the print is a scenario, not this print.

findings.finding: Seven Section 16 initial statements (Form 3) were filed for Gamehaus insiders with event date 2026-03-18, including founder-level CTO/director/10% owner Yan Xi reporting 5,314,953 Class A shares through Joystick Holding Limited -- people who have been insiders since the January 2025 listing -- even though foreign private issuers are exempt from Section 16 and the company continued to file 6-Ks and a Form F-3 afterwards.
findings.adversary_note: I verified this precisely, including the specific document: Yan Xi's Form 3, event date 2026-03-18, reports 5,314,953 Class A ordinary shares held indirectly through Joystick Holding Limited, with Director / 10% Owner / Chief Technology Officer boxes checked. Six Form 3s were filed 2026-03-18 and a seventh on 2026-04-03, and the company did subsequently file 6-Ks and, on 2026-07-28, a Form F-3 — a form only a foreign private issuer may use. So the anomaly is real. It is also worth exactly nothing to this print. A Form 3 is an initial statement: it reports no transaction, no purchase, no sale and no change in holdings, only that a pre-existing insider now has a filing obligation. There is no cash flow, no dilution and no disclosure content in it. And the natural bearish reading — that Gamehaus lost foreign private issuer status and must convert to 10-K/10-Q — does not survive the dates: FPI status is tested on the last business day of the second fiscal quarter, 2025-12-31 for a June year end, and a failure there takes effect on the first day of the next fiscal year, 2026-07-01, not 2026-03-18; and the F-3 filed 2026-07-28 is direct evidence the company still considers itself an FPI. The most parsimonious explanation is a counsel-side filing error or a prophylactic filing, which is a governance-hygiene datum with no valuation content and no path to Sep 8. Nothing in the Q4 release will confirm or deny it.

findings.finding: Neither of the two most material press releases of 2026 was ever furnished on Form 6-K: EDGAR full-text search returns zero hits for 'Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026' under CIK 0002000530 while the same search for 'Second Quarter of Fiscal 2026' returns two, so the last EDGAR-visible revenue datapoint for GMHS is US$26.3m for the December 2025 quarter and the June 8 Q3 release and August 12 strategy change exist only on the wires.
findings.adversary_note: I ran the search myself and the factual core is correct: EDGAR full-text search for 'Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026' under CIK 0002000530 returns zero hits, 'Fiscal 2026' returns only the 2025-11-25 and 2026-03-23 6-Ks, the complete 6-K list has nothing on or near 2026-06-08 or 2026-08-12, and the last EDGAR-visible revenue datapoint is indeed the US$26.3m December 2025 quarter in the 2026-03-23 exhibit. That is a genuine, unwritten observation and it is why this is not an 80. But the inference it carries — that the market therefore cannot see the numbers — is refuted by the record. The 2026-06-08 Q3 release is on PR Newswire, TradingView, Manila Times, StockTitan, Globe and Mail, thestockobserver, scanx and grafa, and Benzinga published the full call transcript. The 2026-08-12 release is on PR Newswire, AOL and StockTitan. Anyone with a newsfeed has both. Nor is the omission clearly irregular: Rule 13a-16 requires an FPI to furnish information it makes public under home-country law, files with an exchange, or distributes to security holders, and many FPIs do not 6-K interim press releases; Nasdaq's public-disclosure obligation is satisfied by PR Newswire. So the premise that this is a compliance lapse is itself contestable. Most importantly, this claim is a transmission mechanism, not a driver: it is the reason GMHS#0 and GMHS#1 might be under-absorbed, and it has no independent effect on the Sep 8 price. Nothing in it resolves at the print.
